name: Binary Exploitation & Reverse Engineering
tagline: Debug, disassemble, decompile, and understand binaries — your own code, lab targets, and CTF challenges.

tools.name: GDB
tools.desc: The GNU Debugger — breakpoints, watchpoints, register/memory inspection, and scripting for any ELF or Mach-O binary you control.
tools.when: The backbone of all dynamic work here; run it plain for a minimal setup or host pwndbg/GEF on top of it.

tools.name: pwndbg
tools.desc: GDB plugin adding exploit-focused conveniences: heap/stack/register views, ROP-gadget search, cyclic pattern generation, and prettier disassembly.
tools.when: Drop it into GDB for CTF pwn challenges or when reversing a binary you own, to spot useful gadgets and mitigations instantly.

tools.name: GEF
tools.desc: Standalone, dependency-light GDB plugin (a single script) with heap visualizations, format-string helpers, and live memory introspection.
tools.when: Want the pwndbg-style workflow with zero setup beyond one curl command, on any GDB build.

tools.name: LLDB
tools.desc: LLVM's debugger, well integrated with Mach-O binaries, clang-generated debug info, and Swift/Objective-C symbols.
tools.when: Analyzing Apple-platform binaries or anything built with the LLVM toolchain where GDB support lags.

tools.name: Frida
tools.desc: Dynamic instrumentation toolkit that injects JavaScript into a running process (yours or a lab/CTF target) to hook functions and read live memory without recompiling.
tools.when: Trace calls, intercept functions, or inspect a live process dynamically — especially on targets where GDB struggles.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.desc: NSA's free reverse-engineering suite with a GUI and a real decompiler that emits C-like pseudocode from machine code, plus a scriptable API.
tools.when: Full static analysis of a binary you own or a CTF challenge — the decompiler output reads far closer to source than raw disassembly.
tools.install: Download the current release zip from the GitHub releases page, unzip, and run ./ghidraRun

tools.name: radare2
tools.desc: Command-line reverse-engineering framework with an analyzer, disassembler, and ESIL emulation, scriptable via r2pipe.
tools.when: Headless or scripted analysis, quick on-box triage, and when everything should live in one terminal tool.

tools.name: rizin
tools.desc: Community fork of radare2 aiming for a cleaner, better-tested codebase while staying command-compatible and offering rz-pipe scripting and Rust bindings.
tools.when: Same CLI workflow as radare2 when you prefer the actively focused fork or need its language bindings.

tools.name: Cutter
tools.desc: Qt GUI front-end for the Rizin reversing engine giving point-and-click disassembly, patching, and analysis in a visual workspace.
tools.when: Visual exploration and annotation of binaries without a terminal-heavy workflow.

tools.name: pwntools
tools.desc: CTF pwn toolkit providing packing (p64/u64), ELF parsing, cyclic patterns, ROP-chain builders, and managed local/remote I/O for exploit prototyping.
tools.when: Prototype and test exploit behavior against binaries in a lab or CTF; the standard glue for the whole workflow.

tools.name: angr
tools.desc: Python binary analysis framework using symbolic/concolic execution to explore paths and solve constraints against a binary you control.
tools.when: Automated pathfinding — such as deriving inputs that satisfy checks — when manual reversing is too slow.

tools.name: Ropper
tools.desc: Python tool that inventories ROP gadgets and builds chains from ELF, PE, and Mach-O binaries; also powers the ROP search inside pwndbg.
tools.when: Quick gadget inventory of a binary in a lab to audit what sequences are constructible.

tools.name: one_gadget
tools.desc: Matches libc builds to single-address execve('/bin/sh') gadgets whose register constraints are simple to satisfy.
tools.when: You have a libc build in a lab or CTF and want short candidate gadget addresses before scripting the constraints.

tools.name: checksec
tools.desc: Bash/Python script that reads ELF headers and reports the active mitigations: PIE, NX, canaries, RELRO, Fortify, and more.
tools.when: First move on any binary in a lab or CTF — establish the mitigation baseline before choosing deeper tooling.

tools.name: file
tools.desc: Identifies a file's type by reading magic bytes and headers, including the format and target architecture (e.g. ELF 64-bit x86-64).
tools.when: Instant triage of any unknown artifact to confirm what you are looking at before deeper analysis.

tools.name: strings
tools.desc: Prints printable character sequences from a binary, exposing embedded literals, format strings, and library references without executing it.
tools.when: Grab a quick inventory of interesting strings — prompts, /bin/sh, format specifiers — before disassembling.

tools.name: objdump/readelf
tools.desc: binutils disassembler and ELF reader: symbol tables, sections, headers, dynamic imports, and per-arch disassembly of your own binaries.
tools.when: Zero-dependency static lookups — grep symbols, inspect section layout, or dump disassembly without a full RE suite.

tools.name: xorsearch
tools.desc: Finds payloads XORed with single-byte or multi-byte keys by matching against known plaintext strings inside packed or obfuscated binaries.
tools.when: Spot obfuscated strings or embedded shellcode in a lab binary — like strings, but for the XOR layer.
